title: Combinations
statement: Return all combinations of k different numbers chosen from 1..n, in any order.

hints.1_question: A combination is an unordered selection. How can you make sure {1,2} and {2,1} are produced only once?
hints.2_nudge: Always pick numbers in increasing order: after choosing i, only consider numbers greater than i.
hints.3_big_hint: bt(start): if len(cur) == k record a copy; for i in range(start, n+1): append i, bt(i+1), pop.

known_bugs.name: may pick the same number again (bt(i))
known_bugs.followup: Should [1, 1] be a valid combination of different numbers?

known_bugs.name: restarts from 1 each time (permutations)
range excludes n
known_bugs.followup: Is n itself one of the numbers you may choose? What does range(start, n) stop at?

followups: How can you prune when there aren't enough numbers left to fill k slots?
How do combinations relate to subsets (problem 78)?
